messages:
Sam: Heads-up — canary rollout for the stricter fncall schema started in eu-west. Seeing ~0.4% toolcall rejects, a few tied to a large customer. @Maria @Noah can you confirm if the console shows route mapping for these rejects?
Maria: Quick check — dashboard shows a sampling spike at 09:12 UTC. Route IDs present but a bunch of rejects are tagged with fallback_route=degen-variant. Screenshot in thread: https://redwood.internal/s/abc123
Noah: Logs: parser errors coming from the email-verifier adapter. Error message: "expected OBJECT but got ARRAY at attachments". Looks like model returned an array for attachments in some responses and our validator fails hard.
Linda: Ugh. If it's an array-vs-object mismatch we can either relax the schema or add an adapter that coerces single-element arrays into objects. Which do we prefer? :thinking_face:
Sam: We should avoid a long permissive roll-back. Two concerns: (1) telemetry / attribution — our fncall reject metric doesn't always include route_id so hard to trace; (2) billing — retries or coercions might double-count toolcalls if we just replay.
Maria: Proposal: add a gateway adapter that does a best-effort normalize: if attachments is an array and length==1 -> coerce to object and add meta `coerced_attachment:true`. Also emit a telemetry tag `coercion=attachment-array->object`.
Maria: Example validator change I sketched:
```{"type":"object","properties":{
  "attachments": {"oneOf":[{"type":"object"},{"type":"array","items":{"type":"object"}}]}
}}```
Noah: I like the adapter + tag approach. Keeps validator strict while giving ops observability. For billing: mark the coerced attempt as a non-billable normalization step and only bill if the normalized payload is forwarded to upstream tool. That avoids double charges.
Linda: We can add `coercion_replay_unbilled=true` flag in the routing policy. Console needs a UX change to show `coercion` reasons on the canary rollouts page. I'll open a console ticket and ping @Console Team.
ops-bot: alert: fncall_reject_rate 0.42% (5m avg) — sampling traces collected (trace_ids: t-9a7, t-9a8). See /alerts/1745559999
Sam: Good. Action items:
- Noah to implement gateway adapter + telemetry tag (PR branch: fix/coerce-attachments)
- Maria to add validator union schema and update canary test set
- Linda to create console ticket to display coercion flags and coordinate billing flag rollout
I'll patch the canary to enable soft-validate fallback for eu-west while we patch adapters. :thumbsup:
Noah: I'll open the PR and add tests for array-of-length-1 -> object coercion. Will tag QA and link e2e traces.
Maria: Adding a sampling rule so these coerced events are kept for 7 days. Also will add an alert threshold if coercion > 0.2% for 15m.
Linda: Ticket created: https://redwood.internal/tickets/PLT-4821 — console page + billing flag. Assigning to @Console Team and @Billing.
Sam: Thanks all. Keep this thread updated on rollout status and whether rejects drop after adapter deploy.
Noah: quick note — when we coerce, include `X-Coercion-Source: gateway-v1` in the forwarded payload headers so downstream tools can opt-in to tolerant parsing.
Maria: Nice. I'll include that header in telemetry events. :white_check_mark:
